messages:
alex_support: heads up — Acme reported a streaming session that disconnected mid-response and client got only a partial chunk. They attached a pcap and a trace id. customer says they retried and were charged twice. sending summary and artifacts below.

alex_support: symptoms: SSE stream opens (200), then several data events, then abrupt connection close after ~4s, client reconnects, gets resume token, but resumed stream misses final tokens. customer attached pcap + server trace id `trace-0a1b2c3d`.

alex_support: immediate ask: can eng/sre help triage connectivity vs runtime drop vs auth rotation? also we need a quick billing check on duplicate billing for partial + retry.

maria_sre: thanks. dropping a checklist: 1) correlation id from customer? 2) pcap location? 3) server side logs for the instance that served the session. 4) proxy / lb timeouts. 5) resume-token TTL and resume-handler logs. 6) metrics: connection_count, conn_close_reason, http_5xx_by_path, stream_error_rate.

alex_support: corr id they gave is `corr-7e9f2a`. pcap uploaded to internal S3: https://s3.redwood-internal/acme/pcaps/session-1950004321.pcap.gz (they also attached a small text trace: /traces/trace-0a1b2c3d.json).

jin_eng: looking now. quick log grep I want us to run:
```
# on gateway nodes
sudo journalctl -u redwood-edge --since "2026-02-12 10:00" | grep "corr-7e9f2a" -A 50 -B 10
# on runtime nodes
sudo journalctl -u inference-worker --since "2026-02-12 10:00" | grep "trace-0a1b2c3d" -A 200
```

jin_eng: curious if this is the known case where the edge returns a FIN after 4s due to upstream idle timeout combined with large unflushed buffer. can someone check nginx keepalive / proxy_read_timeout change from last deploy?

deploy-bot: deploy event: edge-proxy config rolled out at 1950003000 by ops (change id: cfg-edge-2026-02-11-iod). changed `proxy_read_timeout` from 60s -> 5s in staging for load testing (unexpectedly promoted).

maria_sre: whoa — that aligns. if proxy_read_timeout was shortened, it would close connections that are idle from proxy perspective even if worker still streaming small intervals. but customer saw data events before close, so we need to check event pacing and whether proxy considers stream idle.

alex_support: customer says events were frequent (token bursts) but with intermittent 200ms gaps. maybe those gaps exceed 5s timeout? they said it closed after ~4s though — borderline.

jin_eng: grabbing pcap now. quick tcpdump excerpt from pcap:
```
14:02:12.123 IP client -> edge 10.0.0.1: Flags [P], seq 12345:12412, ack 9876, win 412
14:02:16.456 IP edge -> client 10.0.0.1: Flags [RST], seq 8888, ack 11111, win 0
```

jin_eng: RST from edge at ~16.456 — that looks like an active close. need to map which process sent it — kernel or nginx? check conntrack logs + edge socket closer logs.

maria_sre: also check resume token handling. if client reconnected and used resume token but server hasn't flushed final tokens to storage, resume could skip or duplicate. grep resume-service logs: `resume-handler` prints lines like `resume:session=<id> token_ok=true last_seq=58`.

alex_support: billing side: opened ticket BILL-4521 with finance. customer claims duplicate charge on retry. note: our billing counts tokens emitted by runtime; if a client reconnects and server re-emits tokens from seq N, those tokens may be billed twice. we need to confirm whether billing pipeline dedups resume replays.

jin_eng: to reproduce locally, try this curl script that simulates client reconnect with resume token:
```
# open initial stream
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/stream?model=rtx-13b"  --output - | sed -n '1,80p'
# simulate mid-stream disconnect, then re-open with resume
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/stream?resume_token=<token>"  --output - | sed -n '1,80p'
```

jin_eng: also started a pcap replay locally with `tcpreplay` against staging-proxy to see if proxy emits RST on mid-stream bursts. will report.

ingest-bot: metric snapshot at 1950004330: 
- stream_open_rate: 3/s
- stream_close_reason: RST 18 (45%), client_close 34% , timeout 7%
- stream_partial_output_rate: 0.12%
- resume_attempts_success: 92%
- avg_inter_event_gap_ms: 420

maria_sre: avg gap 420ms — well below 5s. but the 45% RST fraction is high. need to see per-instance breakdown; maybe one faulty edge node is sending RSTs. run `edge-node-metrics | jq '.nodes[] | select(.rst_rate > 0.1)'

jin_eng: ok found node e-07 with RST spikes around the time. pulling its logs:
```
2026-02-12T14:02:16Z ERROR nginx[pid=2345] upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.34, server: api.redwood-hosted
2026-02-12T14:02:16Z info kernel: conn_close: socket 0x7f1 closed by process 2345 (nginx)
```

maria_sre: confirms edge timed out waiting for upstream chunk -> nginx closed connection. but why would nginx decide upstream idle? our workers are pushing small chunks but maybe with long GC pauses or expensive tokens. need to check worker-side latencies around that trace.

jin_eng: runtime trace shows a 1.8s stall at token generation due to cache miss and a synchronous disk read for quantized matmul fallback — that caused a 1.9s pause. combined with inter-event gap could have exceeded nginx `proxy_read_timeout` if it was set to 2s somewhere.

maria_sre: deploy-bot indicated config changed to 5s earlier but maybe another layer (internal edge) had 2s. we need full config audit. I'll open a config-audit task.

alex_support: customers asking for mitigation ASAP. options: 1) revert timeout change on edge nodes, 2) increase proxy_read_timeout globally to 60s as before, 3) adjust worker to flush heartbeat events every 1s to keep proxy alive, 4) implement soft keepalive SSE comment ping every 2s.

jin_eng: quickest mitigation is to push heartbeat (SSE `: ping`) from runtime every 1s until final tokens done. patch rolling now to staging. code snippet I'm testing: 
```
// before streaming loop
sendEvent(": ping\n\n");
// and inside generator: flush after each chunk
res.flush();
```

maria_sre: also want to add an alert that monitors RST spike per node > 10/min and correlate with deploys.

alex_support: for billing: finance says hold charges for related sessions until we confirm duplication. Bill team will ingest runtime token logs and dedup by `session_id + token_seq`. I assigned BILL-4521 to finance and support to update customer.

jin_eng: reproduction notes: I replayed pcap against staging-proxy with current edge config and reproduced RST at same point. When I force heartbeat every 1s it no longer closes. so this is likely proxy idle timeout interaction + occasional worker stalls.

maria_sre: long term: patch runtime to ensure heartbeats and also add backpressure awareness so we don't block >500ms synchronous work in token path. Also revert accidental staging->prod config promotion for `proxy_read_timeout`. Ops pls confirm roll back.

deploy-bot: rollback task created: rollback-cfg-edge-1950004600, will queue for immediate rollout.

alex_support: next steps for support: - update Acme with interim mitigation (heartbeat + rollback planned) - ask them to retry after rollback and confirm partial output resolved - update billing ticket that charges are on hold and we'll reconcile duplicate tokens.

maria_sre: I'll follow up with an RCA after rollback + metric stabilization. include timeline, root cause (timeout config + worker stall), remediation (heartbeat, config audit, alert), and customer impact.

alex_support: thanks team. I'll post a short customer-facing note and link to this thread.

ingest-bot: artifact pointers: pcap https://s3.redwood-internal/acme/pcaps/session-1950004321.pcap.gz, server-trace https://traces.redwood/trace-0a1b2c3d.json, edge-logs: gs://edge-logs/e-07/14-02-16.log.gz

alex_support: closing loop — Acme acknowledged mitigation plan and will wait for rollback. will re-open if they see issues after rollback. :thumbsup:
